jobs.description:
Director, CX AI Delivery 
 Who We Are 
 Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture
 With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

 From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

 Location & Flexibility 
 This role will operate remotely in the United States or Canada OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.
 This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

 This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

 This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.
 Responsibilities 
 Strategic Account Governance & Growth 
 Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).

 Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.

 Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.

 Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

 Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation 
 Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.

 Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.

 Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.

 Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.

 Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.

 Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

 Leadership & Talent Development 
 Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.

 Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.

 Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

 Operational & Financial Stewardship 
 Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.

 Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.

 Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.

 Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

 Qualifications 
 10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.

 Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.

 Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.

 Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.

 Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.

 Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.

 Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.

 Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.

 Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.

 Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.

 Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

jobs.title: VP, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
About ClearGov 

 ClearGov is building the modern financial operating layer for the public sector. 

 We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities. 

Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow.

 Our Core Values 

 Be Clear & Credible  

 We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage. 

 Be Human   

 We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength.

 Be Better Together   

 We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier.

 Be Honourable/Honorable   

 We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do.

 Be Connected 

 We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong.

 What Makes You a Great Fit 

 You take ownership and follow through

 You communicate clearly and effectively

 You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out

 You learn quickly and adapt as things change

 You care about the team, not just your own work

 You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

 About the Opportunity 

 We are seeking a hands-on Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis to own enterprise-wide planning, forecasting, and performance analytics for a growth-stage SaaS business. This is not a purely oversight role, the VP, FP&A will be in the models directly, building and stress-testing scenarios, and translating the numbers into decisions. Reporting to the CFO, this person will be a key partner to executive leadership and business unit owners, and will play a central role in the company's next chapter of growth.

 We're looking for someone who wants to build, not just review, someone as comfortable inside the mechanics of a model as they are presenting its output to the CFO and board. 

 Key Responsibilities: 

 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including FP&A leadership, with a track record of being genuinely hands-on in the model — not several layers removed from it.

 Direct experience in a SaaS or recurring-revenue business, fluent in ARR, NRR, churn, cohort, and unit economics analysis.

 Strong financial modeling and scenario-planning skills — able to build complex models from scratch and pressure-test assumptions in real time.

 Exposure to an exit, sale process, recapitalization, refinancing, or similar transaction, with a working understanding of what "diligence-ready" actually looks like.

 Executive presence — able to move fluidly between deep model work and clear, confident presentation to the CFO and board.

 Strong judgment about what's urgent, what's important, and what can wait — able to prioritize across competing asks from the CFO, business leaders, and the sponsor.

 Nice-to-haves: 

 M&A diligence or post-acquisition integration experience.

 CPA, CFA, or MBA.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
JOB PURPOSE 
 Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization. 

 The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement. 

 KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals. 
 Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness. 
 Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options. 
 Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes. 
 Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks. 
 AI Solution Development & Implementation Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities. 
 Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working. 
 Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement. 
 Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured. 
 Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk. 
 AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption. 
 Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks. 
 Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements. 
 Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed. 
 Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required. 
 Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users. 
 Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI. 
 Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support. 
 Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement. 
 Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption 
 Vendor, Technology & Partner Management Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership. 
 Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization. 
 Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation. 
 Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value. 
 QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. 
 Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption. 
 Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization. 
 Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI. 
 Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance. 
 Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.  
 Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset. 

 PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office) 
 Fast paced office environment 
 Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

jobs.title: CFO/VP Finance
jobs.description:
Vice President, Finance and 
Administration / Chief Financial Officer

Division: Finance and Administration

Reports To: President

Direct Reports:

• Controller

• Executive Director, Procurement and Administrative Services

• Executive Director, Public Safety

• Executive Director, Facilities Management

• Internal Auditor

 Position Summary 

Our post-secondary education client is seeking an accomplished and 
strategic financial executive to serve as its next Vice 
President, Finance and Administration / Chief Financial Officer.

As the chief financial and administrative officer and a member 
of the President’s Cabinet, the CFO provides executive 
leadership, strategic direction, and institutional stewardship 
for the school's financial operations, administrative services, 
public safety, and facilities.

This position ensures the responsible management of 
institutional resources while advancing the school's mission, 
vision, and strategic priorities. Serving as a trusted advisor 
to the President, the CFO helps shape institutional strategy, 
provides sound financial counsel, and partners with executive 
leadership to maintain the school's fiscal strength, operational 
effectiveness, and long-term sustainability.

The successful candidate will bring an institution-wide 
perspective and contribute to college-wide initiatives, 
organizational culture, governance, strategic planning, and 
executive decision-making.

 Executive Leadership Philosophy 

The school's Vice Presidents serve as institutional leaders 
first and functional leaders second. As members of the 
President’s Cabinet, they share responsibility for advancing the 
school's mission through collaborative leadership, strategic 
planning, innovation, and responsible stewardship of public 
resources.

The CFO will balance financial discipline with innovation, 
operational excellence with exceptional customer service, and 
long-term sustainability with the evolving needs of students, 
employees, and the community.

Success will be measured not only by the performance of assigned 
departments, but also by meaningful contributions to the overall 
effectiveness, reputation, and future of the college.

 Core Executive Responsibilities 

 Cabinet and Strategic Leadership 

• Serve as an active member of the President’s Cabinet and 
executive leadership team.

• Advise the President on strategic, financial, operational, and 
organizational matters.

• Participate in institutional planning, executive 
decision-making, and policy development.

• Collaborate across divisions to advance college-wide 
initiatives and strategic priorities.

• Represent the school before governmental agencies, financial 
institutions, professional organizations, and community 
partners.

• Develop long-range financial and operational strategies that 
support the school’s Strategic Plan.

• Evaluate emerging trends, risks, and opportunities affecting 
higher education and public finance.

• Champion innovation, continuous improvement, and responsible 
resource management.

 Organizational Leadership 

• Recruit, develop, mentor, and evaluate executive leaders and 
management staff.

• Build high-performing teams committed to operational 
excellence and continuous improvement.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, 
professionalism, and exceptional customer service.

• Promote employee engagement, leadership development, and 
succession planning.

• Establish measurable goals and performance expectations 
aligned with institutional priorities.

 Stewardship and Governance 

• Ensure responsible stewardship of the college’s financial, 
physical, and operational resources.

• Support the Board of Regents through executive reports, 
recommendations, and presentations.

• Develop and implement policies, administrative regulations, 
and business practices that strengthen institutional 
effectiveness.

• Ensure compliance with federal and state laws, accreditation 
standards, Board policies, and administrative regulations.

• Maintain effective systems of internal control, enterprise 
risk management, and institutional accountability.

 Division Leadership Responsibilities 

 Financial Leadership 

• Serve as the college’s chief financial officer and principal 
advisor to the President on financial strategy, fiscal 
sustainability, and institutional stewardship.

• Provide executive leadership for all financial operations, 
ensuring the integrity, transparency, and long-term health of 
the college’s financial resources.

• Deliver financial analysis and recommendations that support 
informed decision-making by the President, Cabinet, and Board of 
Regents.

• Through the Controller and Finance team, provide strategic 
oversight for:

• Budget development and administration

• Accounting and financial reporting

• Payroll administration

• Treasury, cash, investment, and debt management

• Annual financial audits and internal controls

• Financial forecasting and analysis

• Grant accounting and financial compliance

• State and federal financial reporting

• Financial systems and business process improvement

 Procurement and Administrative Services 

• Provide executive leadership for procurement and 
administrative support operations, ensuring services are 
efficient, compliant, transparent, and customer-focused.

• Promote responsible stewardship of public resources while 
supporting operational effectiveness and service to the college 
community.

• Through the Executive Director of Procurement and 
Administrative Services, oversee:

• Purchasing and procurement

• Contract administration and competitive solicitations

• Vendor relations

• Administrative services

• Auxiliary enterprises, including the campus bookstore, café, 
and merchandise store

• Shipping and receiving

 Facilities Management 

• Provide strategic leadership for the planning, maintenance, 
operation, preservation, and improvement of the college’s 
physical assets and campus environment.

• Ensure facilities remain safe, functional, attractive, and 
supportive of teaching, learning, student engagement, and 
community use.

• Through the Executive Director of Facilities Management, 
oversee:

• Facilities maintenance and operations

• Custodial services and utilities management

• Preventive and deferred maintenance

• Capital improvement, construction, and renovation projects

• Campus infrastructure

• Sustainability initiatives

• Space utilization and facilities planning

 Public Safety 

• Provide executive oversight of the school’s public safety and 
emergency preparedness functions, fostering a secure environment 
for learning and institutional operations.

• Collaborate with institutional leadership and external 
agencies to maintain a comprehensive approach to campus safety 
and emergency management.

• Through the Executive Director of Public Safety, oversee:

• Campus security

• Emergency preparedness and response

• Business continuity planning

• Safety compliance

• Threat assessment and risk mitigation

• Emergency communications and crisis response

 Minimum Qualifications 

 Required 

• Chartered Professional Accountant designation in good 
standing.

• Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, 
Accounting, Public Administration, Higher Education 
Administration, or a closely related field.

• At least eight years of progressively responsible executive 
leadership experience in finance and administration.

• At least three years of senior leadership experience within 
higher education, government, or another similarly complex 
organization.

• Demonstrated experience leading multiple administrative 
divisions and managing complex organizational budgets.

• Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership, manage 
organizational change, and build collaborative relationships 
across a complex organization.

 Preferred 

• Experience within an Ontario college or public higher 
education institution.

• Experience with public-sector budgeting, capital planning, and 
community college funding.

 Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities 

The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to:

• Provide visionary executive leadership while maintaining 
strong fiscal stewardship.

• Develop and communicate long-term financial strategies that 
advance institutional priorities.

• Analyze complex financial and operational issues and develop 
practical, sustainable solutions.

• Build collaborative relationships across the institution and 
with external stakeholders.

• Lead organizational change with transparency, professionalism, 
and integrity.

• Interpret and apply applicable laws, regulations, accounting 
standards, and Board policies.

• Communicate effectively with the President, Board of Regents, 
executive leadership, faculty, staff, students, governmental 
officials, and community partners.

• Lead multiple complex operational areas while maintaining an 
institution-wide perspective.

• Develop high-performing leadership teams through coaching, 
mentoring, and succession planning.

• Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, 
continuous improvement, and exceptional customer service.

• Exercise sound judgment and maintain the highest standards of 
ethics, professionalism, and confidentiality.

jobs.title: Managing Director - Data & AI (Montreal, Canada)
jobs.description:
Founded in 2017, Unit8 is a fast-growing Swiss AI and data analytics consulting and services company dedicated to solving complex problems of traditional industries like automotive, chemical, financial services, manufacturing and pharma. We work with some of the biggest organisations in Europe to solve the challenges that directly affect their business - be it operations, finance, manufacturing or R&D. Since our foundation, we have successfully delivered more than 400 projects and have grown to 175+ talented individuals across 7 office locations.

 Unit8’s mission is to drive the adoption of AI and Data Science in the non-digital industries and to help accelerate their digital transformation. Among its activities, Unit8 dedicates a part of its resources and time on projects that deeply matter to us - that includes collaboration on pro-bono and “engineering for good” causes. You can learn more about what we are passionate about at and on our you can find more useful information about our business and recruiting process.

 Are You the Leader We're Looking For?
 As a Managing Director at Unit8, success isn't just about closing deals — it's about becoming a cornerstone of how we grow and deliver in the Canadian market. You will own both sides of the equation: originating high-value client relationships and ensuring the work we deliver actually moves the needle for our clients. If you've built your career at the intersection of commercial impact and technical credibility, and you're ready to operate with real autonomy in an expert-led environment, this is the role.

 What Success Looks Like in This Role
 This is a senior leadership position for someone as comfortable originating a complex engagement as overseeing its delivery. You shape and close the deal, build relationships and trust, and you stay close enough to ensure the technical execution actually delivers value. You will succeed by:

 Building and converting a pipeline of high-value opportunities in the Canadian market — primarily in financial services — through a network earned over years of credible work in data & AI
 Selling from expertise: clients engage with you because you understand their problem because of your deep problem solving skills and experience not because you have a polished pitch
 Staying embedded in delivery long enough to set the right pace, challenge client assumptions, and keep teams focused on the actual business problem
 Bridging the gap between a senior data scientist and a C-suite conversation — translating technical constraints into strategic decisions and vice versa
 Raising the delivery bar by knowing what good looks like and holding teams to that standard

 What You'll Do
 Leverage your existing network to source, shape, and close high-value engagements in Canada (new logos, not just expansions)
 Translate complex business problems into concrete Data & AI solutions: identify where value can be created, make sure the team is building toward it, and hold the client accountable to realising it
 Lead and shape complex, tech-enabled transformations — from early problem definition through to scaled delivery — ensuring the right technology choices serve the business outcome, not the other way around
 Act as the senior point of contact for key clients throughout delivery, ensuring technical execution stays anchored to business value
 Challenge clients when necessary — on scope, pace, and ambition
 Work closely with our engineering and data science teams, providing business context, removing blockers and coaching them.

jobs.title: Head of Data & AI
jobs.description:
About Burq 
 Burq started with an ambitious mission: to turn the complex process of offering delivery into a simple, turnkey solution. It’s a big mission, and now we want you to join us in making it even bigger. 🚀
 We’re proud to be recognized as one of Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Innovators and a 2025 Inc. Magazine Power Partner, awards that highlight how we’re redefining the future of logistics while empowering our partners to grow.
 Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors like Village Global, the fund whose investors include Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Reid Hoffman, and Sara Blakely, we’ve built a world-class team across the globe.
 We operate at scale but remain small enough for every person to have a massive impact. There’s a lot of important work ahead, and joining Burq means the opportunity to grow faster than ever while doing the most meaningful work of your career.

 Here’s a quick overview of what you will be doing:

 The Role
 We're looking for a Head of Data & AI to build the intelligence that powers Burq. 
 You'll build a world-class data-and-ML platform: the systems that turn data into models which make every delivery decision smarter and agents that automate the work the industry still does by hand. You'll set the strategy, make the hard architecture and modeling calls, ship models into production that move the business, and build the team to do it at scale.
 This is a player-coach role. You'll lead and grow the data and ML team while staying deeply hands-on — making architecture calls, reviewing engineering and modeling work, and ensuring the platform serves both product and business goals. You'll partner closely with the Head of Engineering, and with product and AI leadership on how intelligence shows up in the product.

 What You'll Do
 Data Platform

 Own the full data platform — the warehouse, streaming and batch ingestion, the semantic layer, and BI infrastructure.
 Define and enforce data governance — access management, quality standards, and a well-modeled, trustworthy "gold" layer.
 Make the warehouse the source of truth for operational, product, and financial analytics.

 Intelligence & Machine Learning 

 Build the models that power delivery intelligence — forecasting, prediction, optimization, matching/allocation, and reliability scoring that turn our data into better real-time decisions.
 Stand up the ML systems that make this real and reliable: feature pipelines, training, serving, evaluation, and drift monitoring.
 Design the learning loop — instrument decisions and outcomes so models continuously improve.
 Drive the AI agent initiative to production, partnering with product and engineering on the surrounding workflows.

 Team & Stakeholders

 Manage and grow the data and ML team (starting from a small core) — hire data engineers, analytics engineers, and data scientists/ML engineers as the platform matures.
 Establish a clear intake process for ad hoc data requests so the team works from a roadmap, not in reactive mode.
 Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on data-driven analyses and decisions.

new_jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People. 

 Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.   

 With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.  

 For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.   

 Role Summary: 

As Director, Data Enablement, you will architect and evolve reusable enterprise platforms, tools, and services that help users and applications discover, understand, and securely consume trusted data products.

You will set technical direction for data portals, APIs, software development kits and consumption services; advance adoption across departments; and establish scalable operating practices, architecture standards and engineering excellence. Reporting details were not provided. 
 Accountabilities & Qualifications: 
 CPP Investments’ technology and data functions build secure, scalable enterprise capabilities that support investment, analytics, research and operational needs across the organization.  Assess the interaction of public and private market exposures, providing an integrated view of portfolio opportunities, concentrations and vulnerabilities.
 Provide constructive challenge and independent assessment of strategic allocations, portfolio construction choices and material investment transactions.

 Total Portfolio Analytics & Risk Insight
 Lead enterprise-wide oversight of total portfolio risk across public and private markets, including equities, fixed income, derivatives, real estate, infrastructure, private equity and private credit.
 Monitor macroeconomic conditions, market developments and structural investment themes to assess their potential impact on total portfolio outcomes.
 Lead benchmark governance across asset classes, ensuring benchmarks appropriately reflect mandate objectives, risk exposures and return drivers.
 Oversee stress testing and scenario analysis frameworks, partnering with Investment Management and Actuarial teams to evaluate portfolio and funded-status outcomes across a range of market environments.
 Evaluate portfolio vulnerabilities, diversification benefits, liquidity dynamics and cross-asset interactions through a total fund lens.

 Research & Innovation
 Drive research and thought leadership in portfolio construction, asset allocation, risk factor modelling, diversification and advanced portfolio analytics.
 Advance analytical capabilities related to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and data-driven investment insights, and assess their implications for portfolios, markets and investment processes.
 Lead innovation in cross-asset correlation, tail-risk analysis, scenario design and forward-looking portfolio assessment methodologies.
 Collaborate with technology partners, external experts and industry peers to strengthen analytical capabilities and investment decision-support frameworks.

 Leadership & Influence
 Lead, develop and mentor a high-performing team of portfolio risk and analytics professionals.
 Build trusted partnerships across Investment Management, Finance, Actuarial, Technology, Legal, Human Resources and other key stakeholder groups.
 Translate complex analysis into clear, actionable insights for senior leaders and governance forums.
 Represent HOOPP externally through industry forums, peer collaboration, research initiatives and thought leadership.
 Contribute to the long-term evolution of HOOPP’s Total Portfolio Approach and broader investment risk framework.

 What you bring: 

 A graduate degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration or a related discipline. A CFA, FRM, MBA or equivalent professional designation is considered an asset.
 12+ years of experience in institutional investing, portfolio construction, investment strategy, total fund management, multi-asset investing, OCIO, capital markets or investment risk leadership.
 Deep understanding of portfolio construction, asset allocation, investment decision-making and risk management across public and private markets.
 Experience evaluating complex multi-asset portfolios, including alternative investments and derivatives.
 Strong knowledge of total fund investing, stress testing, scenario analysis and quantitative portfolio analytics.
 Demonstrated ability to provide strategic insights that inform senior-level investment decisions and to exercise sound judgement when constructively challenging established views.
 Proven people leadership experience, including building, coaching and developing high-performing teams.
 Executive presence and exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex analytical concepts into actionable investment insights.
 Experience within a pension fund, sovereign wealth fund, endowment, insurance asset manager, OCIO platform or other sophisticated institutional investor is preferred. Canadian or international pension experience is considered an asset.
 Experience with Aladdin Risk, Ortec or comparable portfolio and risk management systems is considered an asset.
 Coding, software development, data science or advanced quantitative research experience is advantageous.

Why you’ll love working here: 
 high-performance, people-focused culture

 our commitment that equity, diversity, and inclusion are fundamental to our work environment and business success, which helps employees feel valued and empowered to be their authentic selves

 Job Summary: 

 Reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Communications, the Director, Enterprise Communications owns the communications strategy supporting HOOPP's investment activities and the external profile of the Office of the CEO. The role carries enterprise level accountability for how the Plan, the Fund and HOOPP's investment approach are understood by external audiences.

 The Director in partnership with the Vice President, Enterprise Communication sets the direction for investment communications, partnering with Investment Management and other business stakeholders on the narrative around portfolio construction, Fund performance, and market conditions. The Director is also accountable for the CEO's speeches, presentations, thought leadership, and key messaging.

 The role leads through influence, directing cross functional teams and external partners on major initiatives and coaching communications professionals across the organization. It calls for an exceptional writer and strategic thinker who absorbs complex investment subject matter quickly, advises with confidence, and delivers at pace with sound judgement and discretion. Investment and financial knowledge is a requirement of this role to support credibility in the room with investment professionals.

 What you will do: 

 Investment communications
 Own HOOPP's investment communications strategy, including the narrative, messaging architecture and external positioning for the Fund.
 Act as senior communications partner to Investment Management, working with the Chief Investment Officer, asset class leaders and subject matter experts on complex investment topics.
 Translate portfolio, market and economic subject matter, including the Total Portfolio Approach, Liability-Aware Investing and Sustainable Investing, into clear communications for external audiences.
 Lead communications for Fund performance milestones, annual and interim results, program launches, new strategies and significant transactions.
 Direct the key messages, statements, question-and-answer documents, and remarks that prepare investment spokespeople for external and industry engagements.
 Build relationships with external stakeholders and investment community contacts to identify storytelling opportunities.

 CEO and executive communications
 Serve as lead communications advisor to the CEO, accountable for speeches, presentations, speaking notes, and key messaging.
 Develop and steward the CEO's external communications platform and thought leadership agenda, aligned to HOOPP's business priorities and reputation objectives.
 Prepare the CEO and Executive Team for high profile external engagements, including conferences, industry events, panels, and stakeholder meetings.
 Counsel the Executive Team and as required, the Board of Trustees on positioning, messaging, and reputational considerations.
 Lead communications for major organizational announcements, executive events, and enterprise-wide engagements.
 Develop executive presentations, Board materials and briefing packages that meet the standards expected at the most senior levels.

 Enterprise leadership and delivery
 Set the cross-channel approach for the communications programs in scope, informed by organizational priorities and audience insight.
 Direct cross functional project teams, agencies, writers, and external partners on major initiatives, setting direction and holding delivery to standard.
 Coach and mentor communications professionals across the team, raising the collective standard of writing, editing, and counsel.
 Set and uphold quality, review, and approval standards for communications products, including accuracy, brand alignment, and accessibility.
 Define how success is measured for the programs in scope and use those measures to sharpen strategy and demonstrate impact.
 Represent Enterprise Communications on enterprise projects and governance forums, and improve communications processes, tools and standards.
 Manage budgets, agency relationships, and external vendors for assigned programs.

 What you bring: 

 Education and experience
 Post-secondary degree or diploma in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Business, Finance, Economics, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
 8 to 10 years of progressive communications experience, including demonstrated ownership of a communications strategy or program at an enterprise level.
 Demonstrated investment and financial knowledge is required, gained through direct experience in investment communications, capital markets, asset management, banking, pension plans or another institutional investment environment.
 Experience as a communications advisor to C-suite executives, including speechwriting and external platform development for a CEO or equivalent.
 Experience developing executive presentations, Board materials, conference presentations, and strategic communications for senior leaders.
 Experience operating effectively within a complex, highly regulated, or stakeholder-rich environment.
 Experience leading through influence, including directing cross functional teams, agencies and external partners without direct reporting authority.

 Skills and capabilities
 Exceptional written and oral communication, editing and storytelling skills, adapted to diverse audiences and channels, particularly external ones.
 Solid working knowledge of investment and financial concepts, including asset classes, portfolio construction, capital markets, and risk and return, with the ability to read and interpret financial statements and performance reporting.
 Strong business acumen and the ability to understand complex financial and investment concepts 
 Strong critical thinking to assess communications needs and risks relevant to the CEO, the Executive Team, and the Board of Trustees.
 Deep understanding of corporate communications and multichannel storytelling in building and protecting external reputation.
 Excellent judgement, discretion, attention to detail and project management skills, with the ability to hold several senior priorities at once.
 Demonstrated ability to build trust, influence stakeholders at all levels and respectfully challenge perspectives when appropriate.
 Highly motivated self-starter who delivers high-quality work with minimal direction and brings structure to ambiguous problems.
 Demonstrated proficiency with artificial intelligence tools to improve the effectiveness, efficiency, and impact of communications, including content development, insight generation, stakeholder sentiment analysis and channel optimization.

 Assets
 A CFA, CIM, CAIA, MBA or accounting designation, held or in progress.
 Experience communicating on behalf of a pension plan, institutional investor, or other long-horizon asset owner.
